messages:
Anya: Heads-up — saw structured funcall failures in the quant bakeoff. Int8/AWQ run produced invalid JSONs on ~2% of eval prompts, fp16 baseline clean.
Miguel: Can you paste an example?
Anya: Sure — produced by AWQ-int8 build after warmup. Payload below:
```
{"tool":"calendar.create","args":{"title":"Team sync",},"metadata":{...}}
```
Notice the trailing comma and a duplicated key in one case. Parser errors downstream.
Sasha: Huh. That smells like token alignment from partial streaming + kv-cache warm start. When prefix tokens are cached the model sometimes emits a ',' mid-emit?
Cheng: Also check quant kernels. AWQ/GPTQ differ in EOS handling and past-key ordering on our runtime. Could shift token boundaries for structured outputs.
EvalBot: Quick stats from last nightly: fp16 exact-match (struct outputs) 96.8% ; AWQ-int8 93.6% (-3.2%) ; GPTQ-int8 95.7% (-1.1%) ; FP8-ish run 96.2% (-0.6%). Failures concentrated in long-context and multi-tool chains.
Miguel: Are these repros across hosted/dedicated/private? Or infra-specific?
Anya: Reproducible locally and on dedicated. I couldn't reproduce on hosted streaming-off config. Seems related to batching + kv-cache + aggressive streaming.
Sasha: Could be dynamic batching interleaving partial generations. If a request A's cached prefix gets reused but the runtime interleaves emission, you can get stray punctuation.
Cheng: On the kernel side AWQ quantization uses grouped int8 matmul and custom softmax kernels — small fp rounding differences can flip token selection when model is near tie. Structured outputs are brittle.
Anya: Repro script:
```
# repro
python -m tests.repro_funcalls \
  --model awq-int8 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kv-cache true --stream true
```
Miguel: Short-term mitigations? Disable prefix caching for quantized models in rollout? Post-parse tolerant fixes?
Sasha: I vote for two-pronged: 1) Disable prefix/KV cache for quantized variants on canary by default. 2) Add tolerant JSON reserializer as a temporary fallback in SDK to fix trailing commas/dup keys (with logging).
Cheng: And a longer-term fix: add per-token calibration tests in model onboarding. If quantized variant changes token selection distribution in the first 32 tokens for structured tasks beyond threshold, mark as failing.
Anya: I'll open a bakeoff ticket and attach eval diffs + repro. Can someone own the runtime bisect? @Sasha?
Sasha: I can take the bisect. Will start with toggling `kv_cache` and then narrow down kernel variants.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy (canary-2026-03-20-awq-int8) started to region-us-west-2 — monitoring.
Miguel: Please include per-route SLOs in the ticket (structured-output-parse-rate). We need CI gates.
EvalBot: Added a monitoring alert: `quant-struct-parse-drop > 1%` to the observability dashboard.
Anya: Thanks — will add labels `quant-bakeoff`, `funcall-regression`, `onboarding-fail` and assign.
Sasha: FYI, quick patch idea: emit explicit "__EOS__" token at end of tool args during training prompts to reduce ambiguity — might help selection stability.
Cheng: Worth trying but be careful with model semantics. Add to experiments.
Miguel: SGTM. Ping me when ticket is up.
Anya: Ticket created: https://redwood/issue/ML-2345 — repro, diffs, attached logs.
Miguel: Nice — locking this thread, follow-ups in ticket. :thumbsup:
